q: show all questions and answers to date
a: This chat has no earlier exchanges to list — your question is the first one, so here is the Trump-versus-Biden comparison instead, with one caveat: the measured series ends in 2020, so it covers Trump's first term (2017-2020) and cannot score the Biden years at all. On screen are the ten largest measured moves from 2016 to 2020: freedom of movement -19 (90 to 71, the 2020 pandemic restrictions are in that number), effective parliament -16 (78 to 62), freedom of expression -15 (89 to 74), freedom of association -15; the overall 22-indicator index fell from 78 to 72, its steepest four-year drop since the series began three years after your Commencement. For 2021-2025 we have only the 2026 report's findings, not yearly scores: it flags significant US decline across 2020-2025 on seven indicators — access to justice, economic equality, freedom of expression, freedom of the press, effective parliament, judicial independence, free political parties — with all but the last now at 50-year lows. That window straddles Biden's term and the start of the current one, so the report attributes the decline to the period, not to either presidency, and neither can honestly be isolated from it here.
